A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 40 pages of each, including Appendices A–C, support reliable matching of text, equations, figures and tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original ReLU-DAE experiments, memorization-detection benchmarks and image-steering results, including Table 1 and appendix experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The two-layer ReLU DAE, regularized training objective, representation-standard-deviation detector and additive steering procedure are unchanged, including Equation 11 and Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: Both versions use MoG, CelebA, LAION, ImageNet and CIFAR10. The generation, denoising, detection and image-editing scenarios are retained, including the appendix steering examples.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Carlini et al., Wen et al. and Hintersdorf et al. for LAION, and Ross et al. for all three dataset-model pairs. The added citations introduce no evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Table 1 retains AUROC, TPR at 1% FPR and runtime, with 500 memorized/500 generalized samples for LAION and ImageNet and 100/100 for CIFAR10. Training, sampling, feature-extraction and steering settings in Appendix B are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices A and B.4 retain the same noise, separability and optimizer checks, tied-versus-untied analysis, test-image denoising, Jacobian study, duplication experiment and single-layer steering ablation.

E5.justification: Appendix A.1's qualitative random-seed robustness statement is unchanged. Neither version adds run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests; representation standard deviation remains a detection statistic rather than experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1's numerical entries and the figures' quantitative and qualitative results are unchanged. For example, the proposed detector's AUROCs remain 0.987, 0.995 and 0.998 for LAION, ImageNet and CIFAR10, respectively.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, mathematical statements and Appendix C proofs are unchanged in substance. Changing some Lemma/Corollary references to Theorem and rephrasing C.2's existing closeness statement do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a unified representation-based account of memorization and generalization, a prompt-free memorization detector and training-free representation steering. Their scientific scope and novelty claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations of spiky versus balanced representations, duplication-driven memorization and differing steerability are retained. The simplified-model qualifications, separability discussion and SD3.5 steering difficulties are also unchanged.

D1.justification: The first-page Resources field changes from 'To be released' to linked 'Code Repository' and 'Project Website' entries. This adds concrete access information; implementation details in Appendix B are unchanged. The linked resources themselves were not inspected.

R1.justification: v2 adds Tinaz, Fabian and Soltanolkotabi's 'Emergence and Evolution of Interpretable Concepts in Diffusion Models' in the introduction and Yang and Wang's 'Diffusion model as representation learner' in Section 5.3. These modestly broaden attribution without changing the research positioning.

P1.justification: Small edits affect punctuation, proof prose, acknowledgments, dates and cross-reference wording; the section structure is retained. Some new Theorem references mismatch unchanged Corollary/Lemma headings, notably 'Proof of Theorem C.1' above Lemma C.1.

P2.justification: Caption cross-references and limited text/equation reflow change presentation slightly. All 19 figures and Table 1 retain their visual evidence and display structures, with no substantive redesign or relocation.

improvement.justification: Replacing the resource-release placeholder with implementation/project links improves documented access, while two relevant citations improve attribution. These are limited practical gains; the theory and empirical evidence are unchanged. Inconsistent Theorem versus Corollary/Lemma references introduce a small presentation drawback, and the linked resources' contents remain unverified.
